fix: it was impossible, by carrying hay or barley on their backs from a great distance, to supply so large a body of cavalry and so many pack animals
reason: Datives τοσαύτῃ ἵππῳ / τοσούτοις ὑποζυγίοις are those supplied, not the carriers; ἢ is 'or'.

fix: since, without their cavalry, even a fight on equal terms was of doubtful issue for them
reason: καί qualifies τὸν ἐξ ἴσου κίνδυνον; χωρὶς τῶν ἱππέων means lacking their cavalry, not setting it aside.

fix: they may become eager to imitate them [...].
reason: Lacuna after ζηλωταὶ γίνωνται must be marked; keep sentence end. Following 'For what seems…' partly reconstructs the lost governing words.

fix: it is clear that, when the sun sets, the degree diametrically opposite it must rise.
reason: Genitive absolute δύναντος τούτου omitted; τὴν κατὰ διάμετρον refers to μοῖραν (degree), not a sign.

fix: wait there with his force, passing the time as if at [...]
reason: ὡς ἐπὶ * πρεπίου is corrupt; 'quietly' is not in the Greek. Mark gap per convention; translator may annotate.

fix: [...] For the Aetolians alone among the Greeks stood face to face with Antipater
reason: Source breaks after παρασπόνδησις...; γάρ opens a separate fragment. Normalized to [...] convention.

fix: set about attacking Pylus by sea, by force and in breach of treaty
reason: ἐπεβάλοντο = attempted; Pylus was not taken (cf. 4.16). 'Piratical' absent from Greek.

fix: because alone among the Greeks they had resolved, under compulsion, to remain quiet during the Persian invasion
reason: κατ᾽ ἀνάγκην omitted; it is the point of the rhetorical contrast.
Passive διακλαπῆναι regularly means to slip away secretly, escape; 'had not escaped' is correct.

fix: Arsinoe is a city of Libya. [...] The ethnic is Arsinoites
reason: Ellipsis in the Stephanus entry marks omitted text; English joined across it.
